title: GTE... but it's DUCK Chess?
summary: 'Guess the Elo' review of subscribers' Duck Chess games on chess.com: he walks through each submitted game (e.g. Professor K204's 5-move duck opening trap), explains duck motifs (cutting off long-range defences, blocking your own check so the opponent's duck is stuck), then guesses the player's duck-chess rating (he is ~1600; variant ratings start at 1500) and reveals it (Professor ~1700).
rules: Duck Chess (chess.com): after each normal move the mover must relocate a shared neutral duck to an empty square different from its current one.
The duck cannot be captured or passed through; it blocks movement for both sides.
No check/checkmate: the king can be left in check and is captured to win (chess.com duck rules); blocking your own check with the duck is a common trick.
win_condition: Capture the enemy king (or checkmate-equivalent / time). In the video: guess each player's rating within ~20 points.

board.theme_notes: chess.com green board with yellow rubber duck blocker; 1:00 clocks; rating-vs-experience chart in intro.

custom_pieces.name: Duck
custom_pieces.moves: placed anywhere empty after each move (must change square); blocks all

events: Elo guess and reveal after each game
current_impl_issues: Current duck mode auto-drops the duck on the most-blocking square and uses checkmate; real Duck Chess lets the mover place the duck anywhere (must move it) and wins by king capture. GTE (guess-the-Elo) framing optional.
evidence: Transcript 0:01 'reviewing my subscribers games and guessing their ELOs... All of the games are duck chess, a chess variant where players take turns placing a non-capturable duck on a new square... variant rating of 1,500'; 0:38 Professor K204 'opening trap'; 1:15 'put the king in check, but then you intentionally cut off your own check with the duck'; 'I'm only rated about 1,600'; 'He is in fact rated basically 1,700 flat'. Frames (visual_d): green board, rubber duck, 1:00 clocks.
